thread:
omar: quick design check  we've been seeing high IO from background compaction on older nodes. thinking about adding an intermediate "compress-and-keep" step for cold host-backed pages instead of immediately compacting (rewrite) or evicting to host. want to flush out tradeoffs.

marta: interesting. compressing in-place could reduce IO and keep pages resident for a while. what's the compression ratio expectation and CPU cost?

luis: rough numbers from offline trace: compressible pages ~28% of resident pages, median comp ratio 2.1x, but CPU cost per page compress ~1.8ms on x86_64 at our build settings. price depends on page size and algorithm (lz4 vs zstd).

anya: alternative is dedupe/zero-run encode (very cheap) for pages with repeats, then fall back to LZ4 for others. dedupe catches sparse embeddings pages well.

devon: need to consider GC semantics: if we compress and keep a page compressed in host-backed area, we must preserve quick decode paths for hot re-touch; decode latency could add to p50 if misused. maybe only compress pages that haven't been touched for X ms and whose hotness score < threshold.
omar: agreed. propose pipeline: 
  - identify reclaim candidates as usual
  - classify: hot / warm / cold by touch window and kv-cache signals
  - for cold: attempt cheap dedupe -> if successful, mark compressed-dedupe (low cost, stays resident)
  - if dedupe unsuccessful and cpu_budget_available -> run LZ4 compress and keep; else enqueue for compaction/evict.

marta: how do we track cpu_budget_available? We already have compaction_score; perhaps add a compression_budget_pct (fraction of spare CPU we can use per node). default 0.07 (7%).

luis: also need telemetry for decode latency: compressed_page_decode_ms (p50/p95) per algorithm + compression_success_rate.

anya: edge case: pages shared across tenants (read-only model weights) we should never compress in a way that breaks sharing semantics. for shared pages prefer dedupe-safe encodings only.
devon: good catch. also need durable metadata to know page encoding type in page descriptor and a fast path when page is in GPU KV cache (avoid double decode). If page is cached in GPU, skip compression entirely.
omar: API sketch (Private YAML):

```yaml
compression:
  enabled: true
  algorithms: [dedupe, lz4]
  dedupe_threshold_ms: 1000  # only attempt dedupe if untouched > this
  lz4_threshold_ms: 5000    # candidate for LZ4 only if untouched > this
  cpu_budget_pct: 0.07
  max_concurrent_compress: 4
  decode_p99_budget_ms: 5     # do not schedule compression that would cause decode p99 > this
```

marta: decode_p99_budget_ms is tricky to enforce; we can approximate by a per-page decode_cost_estimate emitted by compressor and a running EWMA of decode_ms. use that to gate more compressions.
luis: for correctness, compressed storage should support atomic replace: either install compressed blob and update descriptor or do nothing. need a compact atomic switch so readers race safely. maybe a double-mapped descriptor with version tag.

anya: cancelation semantics: if page is re-touched while compression in flight, cancel and mark page hot again. should be cheap to cancel via CAS on a small descriptor.
devon: we also need eviction heuristics if compressed pages still too large or decode overhead too high: prefer evict over decode-heavy pages. set compaction_score to incorporate estimated decode cost: score += lambda * decode_cost_estimate.
omar: measurement plan: stage an A/B canary that enables dedupe-only (cheap) for 24h, collect metrics: compress_success_rate, compressed_residency_change, background_io_bytes, p999 latency. If dedupe looks promising, enable LZ4 with cpu_budget_pct=0.03 and max_concurrent_compress=2 in staging.

ci-bot: canary started: infra/canary/page-compress-dedupe v1 -> staging (job 11555).

marta: defaults I'm ok with for initial RFC: dedupe only on Hosted, with dedupe_threshold_ms=1s, cpu_budget_pct=0.03 for LZ4 disabled. Private can opt-in full algorithm list.
luis: one more: telemetry names we'll need: compressed_page_count, dedupe_hits, lz4_compressions, compression_cpu_ms, compressed_page_decode_ms_p50, p95, p99, compression_cancelations.

anya: perf concern: CPU hot path interference. schedule compression on cores with low affinity to inference threads or use cgroups to limit. Also allow node-level knob to disable compression when cpu_util > 70%.
devon: implementation tasking: need compressor worker pool, cancelable tasks, descriptor CAS, and scheduler integration to check cpu budget and gpu cache. Also tests for atomic install and decode correctness.
omar: action items: (1) luis -> prototype dedupe library and stats (PR #3628), (2) anya -> sketch cancelable worker pool + descriptor format, (3) devon -> wire compaction_score + scheduler gating, (4) marta -> update RFC with defaults and canary plan. target: dedupe-only in staging in 48h.

ci-bot: staging canary reported: 3/3 instances healthy, perf traces uploaded.

marta: comments? if no objections I'll fold dedupe defaults into the RFC later today. :thumbsup:
